# Objectives
* make a dataframe of final host species names (common)
* v2 change: use the v1 table as a start
* complete a lookup of all common names to latin: Genus species 
* fill in the Class, Order, and Family of all taxa
* Make a nice visual of how these all overlap using treemap or similar

# setup
## libs
```{r , message=F}
library(gtools)
library(tidyverse)
library(taxize)
library(treemap)
library(RColorBrewer)
```

## ins and outs
```{r}
## in
# meta.in<-"../04_clean-align/2026-01-12_clean_aligns_wg_out/cleaned_meta/merged_cleaned_meta_HA.csv"
meta.in<-"../../phylo/01_fasttree/ft_rooted_outliers/2026-01-14_rem-outliers/rem_out/trim_nodup_nuc_HA_rooted_resid.csv"

#lookups
lookup.latin.in<-"../../../h5nx_genomic_ml/data/06_host/2025-09-18_out/complete_host_taxa.csv" #this is the lookup from v1 (good start)
lookup.latin.v2.in<-"../01a_ncbi/clean_ncbi/lookups/species_common_latin.csv"
lookup.latin.v22.in<-"../01b_gisaid/clean_gisaid/lookups/latin-common.csv"
#combine all these to have a complete set of lookups from common to latin taxa

# figures out
```


# Read and clean data
## read in latest clean data with host names 
```{r}
#only need meta from one segment
meta<-read.csv(meta.in)
meta$host.old<-meta$host #save original for easy lookup later

#Take only the host common name
meta.h<-meta %>% select(host, host_latin, host.old)
colnames(meta.h)<-c("common","latin.old", "host.old")
```

# Common to latin
```{r}
## Read in the previous table with all species common/latin from meta_clean
commonlat<-read.csv(lookup.latin.in)
commonlat<-commonlat %>% select(-X)

#read in the other two lookup tables (only common host to latin)
commonlatv2<-read.csv(lookup.latin.v2.in)
commonlatv22<-read.csv(lookup.latin.v22.in)
commonlatv2<-commonlatv2 %>% select(-X)
commonlatv22<-commonlatv22 %>% select(-X)
cv2<-commonlatv2 %>% filter(!common %in% commonlat$common)
cv22<-commonlatv22 %>% filter(!common %in% commonlat$common) 

#bind the two (ncbi and gisaid hosts in v2 not v1) together
# cv222<-bind_rows(cv2, cv22) %>% distinct(common, commonold, .keep_all = T)
cv222<-bind_rows(cv2, cv22) %>% distinct(common, .keep_all = T)

# head(cv222)
colnames(cv222) #    common              latin
```

# join lookups to meta, then fill in blanks
```{r}
#1. Join common-latin-lookup to meta by common
meta.h2<-meta.h %>% 
  left_join (commonlat.more, by="common") 

#2. If is.na, look at the old latin (in the metadata, not always to be trusted but sometimes)
#where species is complete, the lookup is there.
meta.nona<-which(!is.na(meta.h2$species))
length(meta.nona) #471
#where species not complete, look at the latin.old (in meta.h2)
meta.na<-which(is.na(meta.h2$species))
length(meta.na) #242
#duplicate this column because we are going to contaminate it with not just speceis, but other latin names
meta.h2$latin.new<-meta.h2$species
these<-c()
for(i in 1:length(meta.na)){
  old.latin<-meta.h2$latin.old[meta.na[i]]
  #is there anything here? if yes, take.
  if(!is.na(old.latin) & old.latin!=""){
    #also check that the old latin is not generic placeholder
    if(str_detect(tolower(old.latin), "ave$|aves$|avian|mammal|other|bird|feline|canine|rodent|bird|duck|ferret|insect|gull|mink|eagle|goose|common|swan|lynx|sandpiper|pheasant|pintail|ibis")){next}
    #should rewrite to lookup common hosts generally
    meta.h2$latin.new[meta.na[i]]<-old.latin 
    these<-c(these,i)
  }
}
meta.h2$latin.new[meta.na[these]] # looks good.

#latin.new is a mix of Genus species, and broader taxa (2-3 words, assume Genus species (subspecies) (unless spp., then Genus))
meta.h2$genus_species<-NA
#for rows where latin.new split on " "  is >1, assign genus species
for (i in 1:nrow(meta.h2)){
  #look to see if it's Genus species 
  hh<-str_split(meta.h2$latin.new[i],pattern = " ") %>% unlist
  
  #If it contains "sp." or "sp$" then remove that from hh. Only genus
  sp<-which(hh %in%c("sp.","sp$"))
  if(length(sp)>0){hh<-hh[-sp]}
  if(length(hh)>=2){meta.h2$genus_species[i]<-meta.h2$latin.new[i]}
  #If length is one... assume it is Genus until proven otherwise
  if(length(hh)==1){meta.h2$genus[i]<-meta.h2$latin.new[i]}
}
meta.h2.back<-meta.h2
```

## Fill in the classifications
```{r}
## Some issues /manual fixes
meta.h2$latin.new<-str_replace_all(meta.h2$latin.new, 
                                   c("Cignus olor"="Cygnus olor",
                                     "Falsco rusticolus"="Falco rusticolus"))

meta.h2$common<-str_replace_all(meta.h2$common, c("Gulls$"="Gull",
                                                  "Domestic cat"="Cat",
                                                  "Turkeys"="Turkey",
                                                  "Cignus olor"="Cygnus olor",
                                                  # "Steamer duck"="Duck",
                                                  "Chicken chicken"="Chicken",
                                                  "Grower"="Chicken",
                                                  "Rooster"="Chicken",
                                                  "Tibetan black bear"="Asian black bear",
                                                  "Mule duck"="Muscovy duck",
                                                  "Savannah cat" = "Leptailurus serval",
                                                  "Knot wader"="Calidris tenuirostris"))

# only fill in where there is no data already

#NA in class means the lookup is complete:
# meta.h2[which(is.na(meta.h2$species) & (!is.na(meta.h2$class))),c(taxa,"common")] %>% head(n=10)
meta.h2.nc.lat<-meta.h2 %>% 
  filter(is.na(class)) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(latin.new)) #use latin where available.

meta.h2.nc.com<-meta.h2 %>% 
  filter(is.na(class)) %>% 
  filter(is.na(latin.new)) #else use common

#set up API and key
taxize::use_entrez()
#setup api key with NCBI/ORCID
#usethis::edit_r_environ()
#ENTREZ_KEY='youractualkeynotthisstring'
taxize_options(ncbi_sleep = 0.5)
# try<-classification(meta.h2$common[1:10], db = 'ncbi', batch_size=5)
# taxa.index<-match(taxa, try[[1]]$rank)
# try[[1]]$name[taxa.index]
#keep log of choices for reproducibility
#only run this where taxa are incomplete

classes.lat<-classification(meta.h2.nc.lat$latin.new, db = 'ncbi', batch_size=5)
classes.com<-classification(meta.h2.nc.com$common, db = 'ncbi', batch_size=5)

#for elements of output list
for (i in 1:length(classes.lat)){
  #check if any data was pulled
  if(any(!is.na(classes.lat[[i]])==TRUE)){
    taxa.index<-match(taxa, classes.lat[[i]]$rank)
    #pull desired taxa if there is info
    meta.h2[which(meta.h2$latin.new==names(classes.lat)[i]), 
       match(taxa,colnames(meta.h2))] <- classes.lat[[i]]$name[taxa.index]  
  }
}
#then common
for (i in 1:length(classes.com)){
  #check if any data was pulled
  if(any(!is.na(classes.com[[i]])==TRUE)){
    taxa.index<-match(taxa, classes.com[[i]]$rank)
    #pull desired taxa if there is info
    meta.h2[which(meta.h2$common==names(classes.com)[i]), 
       match(taxa,colnames(meta.h2))] <- classes.com[[i]]$name[taxa.index]  
  }
}
```

## Where common didn't work for taxize, use other columns
```{r}
#Envir in its own class and don't give orde/fam/gen/spec
meta.h2$class[which(meta.h2$common=="Environment")]<-"Environment"
meta.h2$class[which(meta.h2$common%in%c("Pet food","Milk","Cattle milk product","Raw food","Raw pet food"))]<-"Food products"

not.called<-which(is.na(meta.h2$class))
length(not.called) #56
# meta.h2$common[not.called]

#for those not called, look in genus_species, then in latin.old
for (i in 1:length(not.called)){
  #is there a genus_species?
  if(!is.na(meta.h2$genus_species[not.called[i]])){
    #Use this as species/latin.new
    meta.h2$latin.new[not.called[i]]<-meta.h2$genus_species[not.called[i]]
  }
  #is there a latin (v2 lookup)?
  if(is.na(meta.h2$genus_species[not.called[i]]) &
     !is.na(meta.h2$latin[not.called[i]])){
    #Use this as species/latin.new
    meta.h2$latin.new[not.called[i]]<-meta.h2$latin[not.called[i]]
  }
  
  if(!is.na(meta.h2$latin.old[not.called[i]]) & #otherwise latin.old?
     is.na(meta.h2$genus_species[not.called[i]])){
    #Use this as species/latin.new
    meta.h2$latin.new[not.called[i]]<-meta.h2$latin.old[not.called[i]]
 }
  #And call remaining taxa
  tax<-classification(meta.h2$latin.new[not.called[i]], db="ncbi")
  
  #fill in colz:
  if(any(!is.na(tax[[1]])==TRUE)){
    taxa.index<-match(taxa, tax[[1]]$rank)
    meta.h2[not.called[i], match(taxa,colnames(meta.h2))] <- tax[[1]]$name[taxa.index]
    next
    }
} #end latin.new loop

# all(meta$host.old %in% meta.h2$host.old)
```

## Read in the curated wiki lookups
```{r}
#REad back in cleaned version
check<-read.csv(paste0("2026-01-27_out/out_mod.csv"))
check<-check[,2:3]
colnames(check)<-c("common","wiki")
#check match
length(which(check$common %in% meta.h2$common))
#join
if(any(colnames(meta.h2)=="wiki")){meta.h2<-meta.h2 %>% select(-wiki)}
meta.h22<-left_join(meta.h2, check, 
                    by="common") #note that only noclass2 will have a join

#For noclass2 run taxize again using wiki
for (i in 1:length(noclass2)){
    #See if can be called
    tax<-classification(meta.h22$wiki[noclass2[i]], db="ncbi")
    #fill in remainder:
    if(any(!is.na(tax[[1]])==TRUE)){
      taxa.index<-match(taxa, tax[[1]]$rank)
      meta.h22[noclass2[i], match(taxa,colnames(meta.h22))] <- tax[[1]]$name[taxa.index]
      }
}

#okeee who's left?
noclass3<-which(is.na(meta.h22$class)) #Nothing called if this is empty
length(noclass3) #0!!!

#check
all(meta$host.old %in% meta.h22$host.old)
```

```{r}
  o<-str_subset(these, "mes$") %>% unlist() %>% as.character()%>% first

  s<-g<-f<-o<-"NA"
}
```

## NA orders 
```{r}
noord<-which(is.na(meta.h24$order))
length(noord) #25
# meta.h24[noord,]

for (i in 1:length(noord)){
  comm<-meta.h24$common[noord[i]]
  if(is.na(comm)){next}
  if(comm%in%c("Unknown bird","Environment","Seabird","Waterbird","Shorebird","Wild bird")){next}
  if(comm=="African barn owl"){ #not its own species
    meta.h24[noord[i],c("order","family","genus","species","common")]<-
      c("Strigiformes","Tytonidae","Tyto","Tyto alba","Western barn owl")  }
  if(comm%in% c("Sebastopol goose","American buff goose","Emden goose","Embden goose","African goose","Pomeranian goose")){
    meta.h24[noord[i],c("common")]<-"Domestic goose"
    me<-which(meta.h24$species=="Anser anser")
    meta.h24[noord[i],c("order","family","genus","species")]<-meta.h24[me[1],c("order","family","genus","species")]  }
  if(comm%in%c("Black-throated crane")){
    meta.h24[noord[i],c("order","family","genus","species","common")]<-
    c("Gruiformes","Gruidae","Grus","Grus nigricollis","Black-necked crane")}
  if(comm%in%c("Scoter")){
    meta.h24[noord[i],c("order","family","genus")]<-
    c("Anseriformes","Anatidae","Melanitta")}
  if(comm%in%c("Crested auklet")){
    meta.h24[noord[i],c("order","family","genus","species")]<-
    c("Charadriiformes","Alcidae","Aethia","Aethia cristatella")}
    if(comm%in%c("Chinese ringneck pheasant")){

      meta.h24[noord[i],c("order","family","genus","species")]<- c("	Accipitriformes","Accipitridae","Circus","Circus hudsonius")}
    if(comm%in%c("American goshawk")){
      meta.h24[noord[i],c("order","family","genus","species")]<-
        c("Accipitriformes","Accipitridae","Astur","Astur atricapillus")}
    if(comm%in%c("Blue fox")){
      meta.h24[noord[i],c("order","family","genus","species","common")]<-

     if(comm%in%c("Eurasian buzzard")){
       meta.h24[noord[i],c("order","family","genus","species")]<-
        c("Accipitriformes","Accipitridae","Buteo","Buteo buteo")}
    if(comm%in%c("White mink")){

  if(comm%in%c("Sapphire mink")){
```

## a few more misplaced genus/family labels
```{r}
meta.h24 <- meta.h24 %>%
  mutate(common2 = str_squish(common), host_old2 = str_squish(host.old),
    # Black-necked grebe: trust common name, overwrite taxonomy
    class  = ifelse(common2 == "Black-necked grebe", "Aves", class),
    order  = ifelse(common2 == "Black-necked grebe", "Podicipediformes", order),
    family = ifelse(common2 == "Black-necked grebe", "Podicipedidae", family),
    genus  = ifelse(common2 == "Black-necked grebe", "Podiceps", genus),
    species= ifelse(common2 == "Black-necked grebe", "Podiceps nigricollis", species),

    # Curlew: genus should be Numenius when common says Curlew
    genus  = ifelse(common2 == "Curlew", "Numenius", genus),

    # Tern row where genus was accidentally set to family name
    genus  = ifelse(common2 == "Tern" & genus == "Laridae", NA_character_, genus),

    # Dove/Pigeon rows where genus was accidentally set to family name
    genus  = ifelse(common2 %in% c("Dove","Pigeon") & genus == "Columbidae", NA_character_, genus),

    #  Finch row where genus was accidentally set to "Passerine"
    genus  = ifelse(common2 == "Finch" & genus == "Passerine", NA_character_, genus),

    # Quail row where family/genus placeholders were used
    family = ifelse(common2 == "Quail" & family == "Phasianoidea", "Phasianidae", family),
    genus  = ifelse(common2 == "Quail" & genus %in% c("Galliformes","Phasianoidea"), NA_character_, genus)
  ) %>%
  select(-common2, -host_old2)

# AND unnecc leading " "
meta.h24 <- meta.h24 %>%
  mutate(across(c(class, order, family, genus, species, common, host.old, eco_group), ~ stringr::str_squish(.x)))

                        genus))
```

# Add ecological groupings
```{r}
meta.h24 <- meta.h24 %>%
  mutate(
    class2  = str_squish(class),
    order2  = str_squish(order),
    family2 = str_squish(family),
    common2 = str_squish(common),
    eco_group = case_when(
      # Non-host / non-organism bins
      class2 == "Environment" ~ "environment",
      # Food/products: dairy is special (per your request)
      class2 == "Food products" & str_detect(str_to_lower(common2), "milk") ~ "dairy",
      class2 == "Food products" ~ "food_product",
      # Invertebrates
      class2 == "Insecta" ~ "invertebrate",
      # Mammals
      # Dairy mammals (cattle/goat) -> dairy
      class2 == "Mammalia" & family2 == "Bovidae" & genus %in% c("Bos", "Capra") ~ "dairy",
      # Marine mammals
      class2 == "Mammalia" & family2 %in% c("Delphinidae", "Phocoenidae", "Otariidae", "Phocidae") ~ "marine_mammal",
      class2 == "Mammalia" & order2 == "Pinnipedia" ~ "marine_mammal",
      class2 == "Mammalia" & common2 %in% c("Sea otter", "Marine otter") ~ "marine_mammal",
      # Companion animals
      class2 == "Mammalia" & common2 %in% c("Dog", "Cat") ~ "companion_animal",
      # Swine
      class2 == "Mammalia" & family2 == "Suidae" ~ "swine",
      # Everything else mammal
      class2 == "Mammalia" ~ "terrestrial_mammal",

      # Birds (Aves)
      # Raptors
      class2 == "Aves" & order2 %in% c("Accipitriformes", "Falconiformes", "Strigiformes") ~ "raptor",
      class2 == "Aves" & common2 == "Raptor" ~ "raptor",
      # Waterfowl
      class2 == "Aves" & order2 == "Anseriformes" ~ "waterfowl",
      class2 == "Aves" & common2 %in% c("Waterfowl", "Waterbird") ~ "waterfowl",
      # Shorebirds (subset of Charadriiformes)
      class2 == "Aves" & order2 == "Charadriiformes" &
        (family2 %in% c("Scolopacidae", "Charadriidae", "Recurvirostridae", "Burhinidae", "Jacanidae") |
           common2 %in% c("Shorebird", "Sandpiper")) ~ "shorebird",
      # Seabirds
      class2 == "Aves" & (
        order2 %in% c("Procellariiformes", "Suliformes", "Sphenisciformes", "Gaviiformes") |
          family2 %in% c("Alcidae", "Laridae", "Stercorariidae", "Phalacrocoracidae", "Sulidae", "Fregatidae") |
          common2 %in% c("Seabird", "Skua", "Arctic skua")
      ) ~ "seabird",
      # Waders (herons/ibis/storks/flamingo etc.)
      class2 == "Aves" & (
        order2 %in% c("Pelecaniformes", "Ciconiiformes", "Phoenicopteriformes") |
          family2 %in% c("Ardeidae", "Threskiornithidae", "Ciconiidae", "Phoenicopteridae")
      ) ~ "wader",
      # Poultry/gamebirds
      class2 == "Aves" & order2 == "Galliformes" ~ "poultry",
      # Passerines
      class2 == "Aves" & order2 == "Passeriformes" ~ "passerine",
      # Generic birds
      class2 == "Aves" & common2 == "Unknown bird" ~ "bird_unspecified",
      class2 == "Aves" ~ "land_bird",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  select(-class2, -order2, -family2, -common2)

table(meta.h24$eco_group, useNA = "ifany")
meta.h24 %>% filter(is.na(eco_group)) %>% count(class, order, family, common, sort = TRUE)

# FINAL LOOKUP including the new eco_groups and with fixed mallard/duck issue (20260618)
write.csv(meta.h24, paste0(f.out, "complete_host_taxa_with_ecogroup.csv"), row.names=FALSE)
```

Host species were classified using both taxonomic and ecological criteria to capture complementary dimensions of influenza A virus (IAV) host structure. Taxonomic labels (class, order, family, genus, species) reflect phylogenetic relationships, whereas ecological host groups were defined to represent shared exposure pathways, habitat use, movement ecology, and contact networks that shape opportunities for viral transmission. Ecological grouping is widely used in IAV research because viral maintenance and spread are structured by functional host guilds such as waterfowl, shorebirds, seabirds, terrestrial birds, and mammals rather than by taxonomy alone, with wild aquatic birds recognized as the primary natural reservoir of IAV and distinct ecological host groups exhibiting characteristic subtype distributions and evolutionary dynamics (https://doi.org/10.1128/MMBR.00097-07
; https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1253820
; https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tim.2014.01.004
). Ecological differentiation among bird and mammal groups has been shown to influence viral diffusion, reassortment, and spillover risk across host communities and environments (https://doi.org/10.1038/nrmicro.2017.118
; https://doi.org/10.1098/rstb.2011.0193
). At the same time, ecological similarity does not imply biological equivalence: host susceptibility and transmission potential are also shaped by receptor distribution, immune responses, and tissue tropism, including variation in α2,3- and α2,6-linked sialic acid receptors across taxa and tissues, and the presence of mixed receptor profiles in some species such as poultry and swine (https://doi.org/10.1038/nrmicro1716
; https://doi.org/10.1128/JVI.73.4.3095-3102.1999
; https://doi.org/10.1099/vir.0.2009/006577-0
). Accordingly, ecological host groups were treated as an orthogonal layer of information to taxonomy, representing transmission ecology rather than molecular host compatibility. In addition to broad categories such as waterfowl, seabirds, shorebirds, raptors, passerines, terrestrial mammals, and marine mammals, we defined a distinct group for lactating domestic mammals (e.g., cattle, goats) and associated milk-derived products, reflecting shared husbandry practices and exposure pathways at the wildlife–livestock–environment interface, which have been implicated in recent cross-species transmission events (https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adk3076
). This combined taxonomic–ecological framework was used to standardize host metadata and to enable analyses that integrate phylogenetic relationships with ecological drivers of IAV transmission and evolution.

```{r}
    labs(x=NULL,y=NULL)+
    theme(legend.text=element_text(size=5), 
          legend.key.size = unit(4,"mm"),
          legend.position = "none")
ggsave(paste0(f.out, "n_samp_order_byHost.old_facet-Mainecogroup_common.tiff"), width=18, height=10)
```

# Treemaps plots
## Prep data
```{r}
# meta2.s<-meta2 %>% 
#   filter(!is.na(species))
meta2.s<-meta2 #keep species this time
meta2.s2<- meta2.s %>% 
  group_by(class,order, family, genus, species, common) %>% 
  summarize(.groups="rowwise",tot=n())

#Orders
# meta2.s2
cc<-meta2.s2 %>% group_by(order) %>% summarize(n=sum(tot))
cc<-cc[order(cc$n,decreasing = T),]
ord.order<-cc$order
meta2.s2$order<-factor(meta2.s2$order,levels=ord.order)
```

## Treemaps mammals
```{r}
#mammals:
meta2.s2 %>% filter(class=="Mammalia")%>%
  treemap(index=c("order","family"),
          vSize="tot",
          title = "Class: Mammalia",
          vColor = "order",
          type = "categorical",
          palette = brewer.pal(n = length(unique(meta2.s2$order[meta2.s2$class=="Mammalia"])),                                name = "Dark2"),
          align.labels=list(c("left", "top"),  c("right", "bottom")),
          border.col = "white",
          bg.labels = 255)

#mammals:order and species
meta2.s2 %>% filter(class=="Mammalia")%>%
  treemap(index=c("order","species"),
          vSize="tot",
          title = "Class: Mammalia",
          vColor = "order",
          type = "categorical",
          palette = brewer.pal(n = length(unique(meta2.s2$order[meta2.s2$class=="Mammalia"])),
                               name = "Dark2"),
          align.labels=list(c("left", "top"),  c("right", "bottom")),
          border.col = "white",
          bg.labels = 255)

#mammals:order and common
meta2.s2 %>% filter(class=="Mammalia")%>%
  treemap(index=c("order","common"),
          vSize="tot",
          title = "Class: Mammalia",
          vColor = "order",
          type = "categorical",
          palette = brewer.pal(n = length(unique(meta2.s2$order[meta2.s2$class=="Mammalia"])),
                               name = "Dark2"),
          align.labels=list(c("left", "top"),  c("right", "bottom")),
          border.col = "white",
          bg.labels = 255)

#colors for families:
#mammals:family and common
meta2.s2 %>% filter(class=="Mammalia")%>%
  treemap(index=c("family","common"),
          vSize="tot",
          title = "Class: Mammalia",
          vColor = "family",
          type = "categorical",
          align.labels=list(c("left", "top"),  c("right", "bottom")),
          border.col = "white",
          bg.labels = 255,
          fontsize.legend =8,
          fontsize.labels = 12)
```
